content.tex: INVESTIGATION MAGIC SQUARES
This investigation looks at ways to make a magic square. A magic square is a grid with a different number in each square.
The numbers in each row, each column or each diagonal all add up to the same total. This is the line total.
Example
This is a 3 by 3 magic square using the integers 1 to 9. The line total is 15.
Row \(2\quad 3 5 7\)
\(3\quad 4 9 2\) Right \(1 2 3\) diagonal diagonal Left Column

parts.text: This is a method to make a 3 by 3 magic square. Example This uses the integers 1 to 9. Step 1 Add one square to each edge to make a cross shape. Step 2 Draw three diagonals on the grid. Each one goes through three squares. Step 3 Write the smallest integer in the bottom square. Write the other integers along the diagonals in order, as shown. Step 4 Move the integers from the outside squares to the empty squares inside and opposite. Completed magic square 8 4 2 1 6 5 9 3 7

content.tex: This is a method to make a 3 by 3 magic square.
\(\frac{Example}{This}\) uses the integers 1 to 9.
Step 1
Add one square to each edge to make a cross shape.
Step 2
Draw three diagonals on the grid. Each one goes through three squares.
Step 3
Write the smallest integer in the bottom square. Write the other integers along the diagonals in order, as shown.
Step 4
Move the integers from the outside squares to the empty squares inside and opposite.
Completed magic square \(8 1 6\)
